operationVocabulary.correctedInP211: This field read 173 when written. The manifest declared 139 then and declares 139 now (82 capabilities, 62 of which declare operations); manifest/domains.json is byte-identical to its P2.10 state, so this was an arithmetic error in the evidence, not a regression. Corrected in place with this note rather than silently, because an evidence file whose numbers change without explanation is not evidence. The count is now generated into .ai/master/CURRENT_STATUS.md.
operationVocabulary.grounding: Derived from real routes in src/rest/routes.mjs and real module exports. Capabilities with no implementation declare [] and keep an honest status rather than being given invented operations.

executionVsExecutions.rationale: Creating a second capability-owning domain to match UI plurality would duplicate ownership for a grammatical difference.

aiFoundation.notImplemented: No inference, no agent loop, no gateway client, no MCP server or client, no vendor SDK, no network call, no daemon, no new dependency. A test asserts exactly one file read (its own manifest) and no fetch/child_process/WebSocket/socket API.
aiFoundation.vendorNeutrality: F15 enforces that vendor names appear only inside `examples` arrays. Verified by deliberately leaking '9router' into a contract id and confirming the gate fired.
aiFoundation.failClosedFixed: requiresApproval() was initially written as list.includes(), which fails OPEN for unknown actions. Caught by my own test run before commit and corrected: unknown => requires approval; read-only must be proven.

bugsFoundByNewWork: requiresApproval() fail-open on unknown actions (mine, fixed before commit)
five stream operations with no backpressure policy, including the editor push stream where a slow browser could grow the server heap — each now has a policy and a recorded reason

a secret scan banned the substring 'secret', which would have forced credentials.external-secrets to be misnamed — replaced with secret-bearing FIELD names and credential-shaped literals
